Ms. Sharmila Sharma, learned counsel for the complainant / objector.

Heard on I.A. No.8323/2025, which is first application under Section 430 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant - Adnan Khan S/o Azad Khan.

The present appellant has been convicted for commission of offences punishable under Section 376(2)(N) of the Indian Penal Code, Sections 3/4 & 5(j)(ii)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to undergo Life Imprisonment along with fine of Rs.1,000/-, 10 years' rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.1,000/- and Life Imprisonment along with fine of Rs.1,000/- with usual default stipulations.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The allegation against the present appellant is that he exploited the prosecutrix physically and out of the same, she got pregnant.
Counsel for the appellant argued that the prosecutrix was the consenting party.
the prosecutrix and her parents have not supported the case of prosecution.
The appellant has been convicted only on the basis of age of the prosecutrix and DNA report.
He also argued that source of recording of 2 CRA-4896-2025 date of birth of the prosecutrix in the scholar register has not been proved by the prosecution.
The age of the appellant was also 18 years at the time of incident.
He argued that the during the trial, the appellant was on bail and it is not the case of the prosecution that he ever misused the liberty granted to him.
Hence, remaining jail sentence of the present appellant be suspended.
Counsel for the State opposed the application.

sentences.text:
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the testimony of prosecutrix and her parents, who have not supported the case of prosecution and also the fact that the source of recording of date of birth of the prosecutrix has not been proved by the prosecution,
though counsel for the State relied on the testimony of Rajeev Kumar Mishra (PW-7) that the birth certificate was brought to the Court, however, from going through the statement of PW-7 & PW-8 in paras - 12 & 13, it is clear that the birth certificate was not produced by the prosecuton, therefore, we find it a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant.

In the case of Tejubai v/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75, it has been held that if the date of birth of the prosecutrix in the school register is recorded on the basis of a person who made entry of the date of birth, the same is not sufficient to prove the age.

entities.text: Tejubai v/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the same, we deem it appropriate to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.8323/2025 stands allowed.

The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant - Adnan Khan 3 CRA-4896-2025 shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal and he be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court and on depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 21.08.2026 , and thereafter, on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.

Certified copy, as per Rules.
 (VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) (ALOK A  JUDGE JUD
